title: Marceline's Lost Song
synopsis: Marceline can remember every song she has ever written except one, and it is the one that matters.
plot:
Marceline is cleaning out old tapes when she finds a label in her own handwriting: 'the good one'. The tape is blank. She has no memory of writing it. She asks Finn and Jake to help her find it, and they spend the day retracing a thousand years of places she has slept.

Simon, when asked, remembers a girl humming in a bombed-out record store, but cannot remember the tune, only that it made him stop being afraid for a moment. Hunson Abadeer, summoned reluctantly, says the song was about him and that he did not care for it, which Marceline accepts as proof that it was good. Nobody can hum it.

Back home, Jake accidentally sits on the bass, and the open strings ring a chord. Marceline freezes. It is the first chord. She plays it, and the rest arrives on its own, a simple lullaby she wrote for herself when she was seven and had no one to sing it to her. She records it on the blank tape. Finn asks what the words are. Marceline says there aren't any. There never were. That's why it was the good one.
transcriptText:
Marceline: 'The good one.' That's my handwriting. And it's blank.
Finn: Maybe you taped over it?
Marceline: I don't tape over the good ones, Finn. That's like a rule.
Jake: So what do we do?
Marceline: We go everywhere I've ever been. Should take about a week.
Jake: A WEEK?
Marceline: I'm a thousand years old, Jake.
[Ice Kingdom.]
Simon: A song? Hmm. There was a record store. Everything was broken. You were humming.
Marceline: Do you remember the tune?
Simon: No. But I remember I wasn't scared, for a minute. That's all I've got, Marcy. I'm sorry.
Marceline: That's a lot, Simon.
[The Nightosphere.]
Hunson Abadeer: Oh, THAT song. It was about me. I didn't like it.
Marceline: So it was good.
Hunson Abadeer: That is not what I said.
Marceline: That's what I heard. Can you hum it?
Hunson Abadeer: I don't hum. I'm the lord of evil.
Jake: Even evil hums, man.
Hunson Abadeer: [trying] Hmm hm hmm— no. No, it's gone.
[Marceline's house. Jake sits down heavily on the axe bass. The strings ring out.]
Jake: Sorry! Sorry, I didn't see—
Marceline: Wait.
Finn: What?
Marceline: Don't move. [She picks up the bass. Plays the chord. Then the next one.]
Marceline: [softly] Oh.
[She plays a slow lullaby. No words.]
Finn: What are the words?
Marceline: There aren't any. I was seven. There wasn't anybody to sing it to me, so I just... made the part that goes underneath.
Jake: That's the good one?
Marceline: That's the good one.
[She presses record.]
